name: Ifrane
hero_subtitle: The charming mountain town in the heart of the Middle Atlas — cedar forests, scenic lakes, crisp air, and the famous Stone Lion statue.

info.best_time_val: May – October (and snow from December – March)
info.entry_val: By road from Fes (1 hour) or Meknes (1 hour)

overview.title: A Breath of Fresh Mountain Air in the Middle Atlas
overview.p1: Sitting at over 1,600 meters above sea level in the Middle Atlas Mountains, Ifrane was built in the 1930s with sloped roofs and European-style chalets. Nicknamed 'Morocco's Little Switzerland,' it stands out for its serene atmosphere, cool summers, snowy winters, and surrounding cedar forests and lakes—all just an hour away from Fes or Meknes.
overview.p2: One day is enough to explore the town center, see the Stone Lion statue, and stroll near a lake and cedar forest. You can stay longer to enjoy mountain hiking or winter skiing at Michlifen. Bringing warm layers is always recommended, even in summer.

places.title: Places to Visit in Ifrane

lion.desc: The famous carved statue in the heart of town, Ifrane's most photographed symbol.

aoua.title: Dayet Aoua

hachlaf.title: Dayet Hachlaf

itinerary.title: Suggested 2- or 3-Day Itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: Explore the town and the Stone Lion first, then head out toward the lakes and cedar forests.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Visit the Stone Lion statue, stroll through the town center, and enjoy a coffee in the crisp air.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Head to Lake Dayet Aoua for lakeside walks and birdwatching.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Dine at one of the town's restaurants, keeping in mind that mountain nights get chilly.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Explore hiking trails in the cedar forests and visit the historic Gouraud Cedar area.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Drive up the hills to the Michlifen viewpoint or stop to unwind by Dayet Hachlaf.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Return to Ifrane for a quiet dinner and relaxation.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Visit Tizguit Spring or Aïn Vittel and take a short walk among the trees.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Explore the edges of Ifrane National Park or admire the architecture around Al Akhawayn University.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Sip a final glass of mint tea before heading toward Fes or Meknes.

1.title: Altitude & Weather
1.desc: The town sits over 1,600 meters high, meaning cool nights year-round and potential snow during winter.

2.title: Getting Around & Driving
2.desc: Renting a car is the best option to freely explore the lakes, cedar forests, and Michlifen; grand taxis are also available from Fes and Meknes.

3.title: Respect Nature & Wildlife
3.desc: Stick to marked trails, leave no litter behind, and avoid disturbing wild animals.

q1.question: How many days are enough to visit Ifrane?
q1.answer: One full day is enough to explore the town center and main sights, while staying two or three days gives you plenty of time for hiking and visiting the lakes and cedar forests.

q2.question: Is the weather cold in Ifrane?
q2.answer: Yes, Ifrane is noticeably cooler than neighboring cities all year round. It has mild, pleasant summers and cold, snowy winters.

q3.question: Do you need a car to visit Ifrane?
q3.answer: Having a car is recommended to easily get around between the lakes, cedar forests, and Michlifen.

q4.question: Can you go skiing in Ifrane?
q4.answer: Michlifen Resort offers skiing and winter facilities when snow falls during the winter season (roughly December to March).

q5.question: How far is Ifrane from Fes?
q5.answer: Ifrane is about a one-hour drive from Fes.
